title: Why we don’t judge risk controls by the next candle - a LIVE BEAR100 case study
author: profittoinvest
selftext:
Hello everyone  
  
On **November 3**, we manually executed one of our portfolio protection rules on the LIVE Profitto Invest account.

The rule is called:

**BEAR100 12H**

It was designed after extensive backtesting covering multiple market regimes, including data going back to **2020**.

The idea is simple::

When BTC confirms a bearish **EMA20/50 cross on the 1D timeframe**, we do not react immediately.

We wait for the daily candle to close, then wait another **12 hours**.

After that confirmation period, the rule closes the remaining LONG positions.

The purpose is not to maximize the result of that specific moment.

The purpose is to reduce portfolio risk when the market regime changes from bullish to bearish.

# What happened this time?

At first, the decision looked wrong.

After the initial decline, several positions had already reached TP3.

Then the market rebounded sharply.

For a while, it looked as if some of the LONG positions we had manually closed could also have recovered and eventually reached TP3.

From a short-term perspective, BEAR100 looked like a mistake.

But we did not change the rule.

That is important.

Risk-management rules are not designed to be judged by the next candle, the next hour or even the next day.

They are designed around the behaviour of the **whole portfolio over longer periods**.

Later, the market reversed again and fell sharply.

The remaining portfolio was already positioned much more defensively, and a series of SHORT positions began closing at TP3.

The bot started recovering from a significant drawdown and moved back toward a rising equity path.

That is exactly what BEAR100 was designed for.

Not to predict the perfect top.

Not to make every individual decision look good immediately.

But to improve the behaviour of the portfolio when the market regime changes.

# Why we use rules instead of intuition

One of the biggest mistakes in systematic trading is changing the rules every time a decision looks bad in the short term.

If a protection mechanism was developed from years of testing, it has to be evaluated across many situations.

Sometimes it will reduce profit.

Sometimes the market will reverse immediately after the protection is activated.

Sometimes doing nothing would have produced a better result.

But the important question is:

**What does the rule do to the portfolio over hundreds of trades and multiple market regimes?**

Our historical testing showed that BEAR100 improves the long-term behaviour of the strategy and reduces the impact of deeper bearish periods.

That is why we keep the rule even when one individual execution initially looks uncomfortable.

# BEAR100 is not our only protection

During an active bearish regime, we also use another portfolio-level rule that limits how much LONG exposure the bot can rebuild.

The goal is to prevent the portfolio from becoming heavily LONG again while the broader market remains bearish.

This still allows new LONG signals to be accepted, but the LONG side cannot dominate the portfolio.

So BEAR100 is not an isolated intervention.

It is part of a wider portfolio-risk framework developed from our historical testing.

# Next comparison: LIVE vs raw strategy

For the period from **July 4 to November 9**:

**LIVE BingX:** \+212.20% return, with an observed peak-to-trough drawdown of approximately **28.2%**.

**Raw Cornix backtest:** \+219.90% return, with **34.49% maximum drawdown**.

The raw strategy finished slightly ahead in return, while the LIVE account experienced a noticeably smaller drawdown.

This does not prove that the protection rules alone caused the difference, because LIVE execution follows a different portfolio path.

However, the result is consistent with their purpose:

**not necessarily to maximize short-term profit, but to control deeper drawdowns and improve the behaviour of the portfolio over time.**

# A note about Cornix Marketplace statistics

We also want to be transparent about the numbers currently visible on our Cornix Marketplace profile.

The Marketplace history still includes periods where the configuration was not aligned with the final production setup.

Because the displayed statistics are updated continuously, those older periods are still affecting the current 1-month, 3-month and 6-month results.

As time passes and the rolling history moves further into the period using the correct configuration, those statistics should gradually become more representative of the strategy we are actually running today.

That process takes time.

For now, anyone can independently verify the strategy by joining **Profitto Invest on the Cornix Marketplace** and running their own backtests using the configuration we publish.

We prefer showing the imperfect history rather than hiding it.

We have also documented our current Cornix setup and portfolio-protection rules on our Discord server.

If you want to see exactly how the bot is configured and how the additional risk controls work:

**The goal is not to make every trade look perfect.**  
**The goal is to build a system that behaves better over the full market cycle.**

comments.body: A risk rule shouldn't be judged by whether the next candle moves in your favor. Its purpose is reducing losses across hundreds of decisions, not predicting every reversal. That principle applies to leveraged wagers on moon too. Sometimes protecting capital means accepting that the market might recover without you.
